# FORTH/Sigma Complete word reference

This reference covers every registered word, standard keyboard constant, optional-library word, parser form and local declaration form in the current implementation, regardless of when it was added. Private library helpers are included and marked separately from the public API. Arbitrary user-defined names are outside this inventory.

Each entry has a stack effect and a behavior description based on runtime HELP, registration sources and implementation definitions. See the [reading guide and examples](WORD_REFERENCE_GUIDE.md) for notation, prerequisites, examples and cautions, and the related manual sections for longer explanations.

Coverage assumes the full build. Feature-disabled builds omit their respective words. Load optional vocabularies with REQUIRE before adding them to the search order. Immediate/compile-only flags come from the built-in implementation; syntax forms have their own conditions in their descriptions.

Entries (namespace/name pairs): **1927**. The same name in different vocabularies counts separately.

### ` ADSR `

` ( attack-ms decay-ms sustain release-ms -- ) `

Set the instrument's envelope as ENVELOPE's segments: a straight attack, an exponential decay to sustain (0 to 65535) held until the note stops, and an exponential release (FORTH/Sigma audio).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-AUDIO ALSO AUDIO ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Instruments](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#instruments).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
7 INSTRUMENT PULSE 16384 DUTY 10 200 40000 300 ADSR
```

[Example context](../src/tests/audio_test.zig#L365)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: ADSR ( attack-ms decay-ms sustain release-ms -- )   SND-ADSR ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_audio.zig](../src/core/words_audio.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1436).

### ` AUDIO? `

` ( -- flag ) `

Report whether an available audio engine reaches a physical device; without a device it runs silently. A host without an audio engine callback throws HostUnavailable instead of returning false.

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-AUDIO ALSO AUDIO ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Sound](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#sound), [Playing](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#playing), [PCM streams](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#pcm-streams).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
AUDIO?
```

[Example context](../src/tests/audio_test.zig#L331)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: AUDIO? ( -- flag )   SND-DEVICE ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_audio.zig](../src/core/words_audio.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1420).

### ` BEEP `

` ( -- ) `

Stop the music and SFX and MOD, set the PLAY settings as at start, and sound about 1316 Hz at V7 for 40 ms on the standard square (FORTH/Sigma audio).

### ` DUTY-STEPS `

` ( n -- ) `

Round the instrument's pulse duty to n steps (never 0 or a whole cycle); 0 for none (FORTH/Sigma audio).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-AUDIO ALSO AUDIO ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [A chip's steps](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#a-chips-steps).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
CREATE LV 0 , 1000 , 65535 ,  LV 3 VOLUME-STEPS 8 DUTY-STEPS 1 INTERPOLATION
```

[Example context](../src/tests/audio_test.zig#L1510)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.


Sources: [src/core/words_audio.zig](../src/core/words_audio.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1733).

### ` ENVELOPE `

` ( addr n loop release -- ) `

Set the instrument's envelope: n (0 to 16) segments of three cells (level 0 to 65535, ms, curve 0 straight or 1 exponential), the segment to loop back to and the one held until the note stops (-1 for none) (FORTH/Sigma audio).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-AUDIO ALSO AUDIO ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Instruments](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#instruments).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
0 0 -1 -1 ENVELOPE
```

[Example context](../src/tests/audio_test.zig#L477)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment. Use valid logical-memory addresses, lengths and capacities; distinguish owned storage from borrowed lifetimes.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: ENVELOPE ( addr n loop release -- )   2 SND-TONE ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_audio.zig](../src/core/words_audio.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1717).

<a id="w-415544494f3a46494c544552"></a>

### ` FILTER `

` ( mode hz resonance -- ) `

Send the instrument through its own filter: mode 0 none, 1 low-pass, 2 band-pass, 3 high-pass, 4 low-pass and high-pass added (a notch), 5 low-pass and band-pass, 6 band-pass and high-pass, 7 all three; cutoff 0 to 1000000 Hz, resonance 0 to 65535 (FORTH/Sigma audio).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-AUDIO ALSO AUDIO ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Instruments](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#instruments), [Modules](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#modules).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
7 100 0 FILTER
```

[Example context](../src/tests/audio_test.zig#L405)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: FILTER ( mode hz resonance -- )   SND-FILTER ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_audio.zig](../src/core/words_audio.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1442).

### ` INSTRUMENT-PAN `

` ( left right -- ) `

Set the instrument's left and right levels, -65535 to 65535 (a negative side is inverted); 65535 65535 at first (FORTH/Sigma audio).

Kind: library.

Related: [Instruments](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#instruments), [All the voices together](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#all-the-voices-together).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)


### ` LOAD-MOD `

` ( c-addr u -- ) `

Load a 4-channel, 31-sample ProTracker MOD into the shared sample pool. Reloading consumes more space until FREE-SAMPLES; invalid modules throw -277, pool exhaustion is out of memory.

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-AUDIO ALSO AUDIO ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Modules](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#modules).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
REQUIRE-AUDIO ALSO AUDIO S" a.txt" LOAD-MOD
```

[Example context](../src/tests/audio_test.zig#L908)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment. Use valid logical-memory addresses, lengths and capacities; distinguish owned storage from borrowed lifetimes.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: LOAD-MOD ( c-addr u -- )   SND-LOAD-MOD THROW ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_audio.zig](../src/core/words_audio.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1462).

<a id="w-415544494f3a4c4f41442d53414d504c45"></a>

### ` LOAD-SAMPLE `

` ( c-addr u n -- ) `

Load 8/16-bit PCM WAV as mono sample n (0..63). Samples and MOD share a 64 MiB pool; reloading a slot consumes more space until FREE-SAMPLES. Invalid files throw -276; pool exhaustion is out of memory.

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-AUDIO ALSO AUDIO ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

<a id="w-415544494f3a504c41592d5245534554"></a>

### ` PLAY-RESET `

` ( -- ) `

Stop MML and its voices as 0 PLAYS does, and put the voices' MML settings (octave, length, tempo, volume, instrument, S and M, P, Y, K, Q) back as at start, without a sound. SFX, MOD, samples, and instruments stay; BEEP does the same with its sound and stops SFX and MOD too (FORTH/Sigma audio).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-AUDIO ALSO AUDIO ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

### ` SND-PCM-CLOSE `

` ( pcm -- ior ) `

Host primitive: Discard and detach, waiting up to 1000ms for consumer acknowledgement. Busy -528 or interruption -516 keeps the closing ID for retry. Success invalidates the ID; host retains backing storage until shutdown.

Kind: builtin.

` REQUIRE-AUDIO ALSO AUDIO ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [PCM streams](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#pcm-streams).

Usage example

```forth
REQUIRE-AUDIO ALSO AUDIO 0 SND-PCM-CLOSE DROP
```

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment. Check the returned ior; zero is success. Passing it to THROW is one option.

Sources: [src/core/words_audio.zig](../src/core/words_audio.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1706).

<a id="w-415544494f3a534e442d50434d2d4f50454e"></a>

### ` SND-PCM-OPEN `

` ( hz channels capacity -- pcm ior ) `

Host primitive: Open one host-owned s16LE mono/stereo stream. Input 8000..192000 Hz; power-of-two capacity 256..65536 frames, 40ms..1s. Busy -528; no storage -524; identity exhaustion -587.

<a id="w-415544494f3a534e442d534e45532d4652414d4553"></a>

### ` SND-SNES-FRAMES `

` ( regs aram voices globals history frames layout -- ) `

Internal synchronous S-DSP kernel. Layout 1 borrows disjoint buffers: 128 bytes registers, 65536 bytes ARAM, 112/10/16 little-endian signed 64-bit cells for voices/globals/echo history. Validates addresses, fields and time before effects; -9 address, -24 layout/range/overlap. Completed frames persist on execution interruption. No audio device or retained pointers. See SNES\_DSP\_NATIVE\_DESIGN.md.

Kind: builtin.

` REQUIRE-AUDIO ALSO AUDIO ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example

```forth
S" include/snes-dsp-audio.fs" INCLUDED REQUIRE-AUDIO ALSO AUDIO SD-REGS SD-ARAM SD-VOICES SD-GLOBALS SD-EHIST 0 1 SND-SNES-FRAMES
```

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Sources: [src/core/words_audio.zig](../src/core/words_audio.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1710).

<a id="w-415544494f3a534e45532d4652414d4553"></a>

### ` SNES-FRAMES `

` ( regs aram voices globals history frames layout -- ) `

Synchronous S-DSP frame kernel; layout1 and five disjoint borrowed VM buffers. See SND-SNES-FRAMES and SNES\_DSP\_NATIVE\_DESIGN.md for exact sizes/fields. Invalid address -9; invalid layout/count/state/overlap -24, before effects. Zero frames changes nothing after validation. No audio device; completed frames persist on interruption.

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-AUDIO ALSO AUDIO ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example

```forth
S" include/snes-dsp-audio.fs" INCLUDED REQUIRE-AUDIO ALSO AUDIO SD-REGS SD-ARAM SD-VOICES SD-GLOBALS SD-EHIST 0 1 SNES-FRAMES
```

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: SNES-FRAMES ( regs aram voices globals history frames layout -- ) SND-SNES-FRAMES ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_audio.zig](../src/core/words_audio.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1755).

<a id="w-415544494f3a564f4943452d484f4c44"></a>

### ` VOICE-HOLD `

` ( instrument hz volume voice -- ) `

Sound instrument (0 to 63) on voice 1 to 16 at hz (in 1/1000 Hz) and volume (0 to 65535) until told otherwise; the same instrument again goes on (its envelope too) at the new pitch and volume with the instrument's settings as they are now, another starts anew, an envelope that ends at 0 keeps the voice at 0, and volume 0 silences the voice. PLAY, SFX, MOD, and stops take their voices back (FORTH/Sigma audio).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-AUDIO ALSO AUDIO ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [All the voices together](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#all-the-voices-together), [The chip libraries](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#the-chip-libraries), [The audio device](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#the-audio-device).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
0 0 0 2 VOICE-HOLD
```

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):


### ` K-ALT-MASK `

` ( -- u ) `

Standard Alt modifier mask. Standard EKEYS modifier mask 536870912 (hex 0x20000000). Use with EKEY/EKEY&gt;FKEY, not with GRAPHICS INKEY. Host support determines which events can be received.

Kind: constant.

` ALSO EKEYS ` selects standard keyboard constants, using an encoding independent of GRAPHICS.

Usage example

```forth
ALSO EKEYS K-ALT-MASK . PREVIOUS
```

Caution: Follow the operand order in the stack effect. Example names and values depend on their setup.

Sources: [src/core/standard_keys.zig](../src/core/standard_keys.zig).

<a id="w-455854454e53494f4e3a434f4d504143542d46494c454e414d45"></a>

### ` COMPACT-FILENAME `

` ( c-addr u -- c-addr u2 ) `

Compact a byte path in place like Gforth 1.0.2, retaining its address. Only slash separates components; terminal dot/dot-dot are retained. Does not access the filesystem or resolve links. Invalid memory/negative length throws -9, temporary allocation failure -257, preserving arguments and source. No fixed 1024-byte limit; files support is not required.

Kind: builtin.

` REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example

```forth
REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION S" a/../b" COMPACT-FILENAME TYPE PREVIOUS
```

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment. Use valid logical-memory addresses, lengths and capacities; distinguish owned storage from borrowed lifetimes.

Sources: [src/core/words_extension.zig](../src/core/words_extension.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1393).

<a id="w-455854454e53494f4e3a454b45592d57414954"></a>

### ` EKEY-WAIT `

` ( ms -- event flag ior ) `

Wait for a complete standard event with one monotonic deadline; zero polls, negative waits indefinitely. Timeout returns 0 0 0, EOF K-EOF true 0. Partial input survives timeout and interruption. Selected files decode UTF-8 with literal ESC and byte 3; host-owned partial bytes remain readable after the scope exits. A missing file-wait callback throws -21.

Kind: builtin.

` REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example

```forth
REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION 0 EKEY-WAIT DROP 2DROP PREVIOUS
```

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment. Check the returned ior; zero is success. Passing it to THROW is one option.

Sources: [src/core/words_extension.zig](../src/core/words_extension.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1371).

<a id="w-455854454e53494f4e3a455845432d4c494d49544544"></a>

### ` EXEC-LIMITED `

` ( i*x xt u -- j*x ior ) `

Debug-only bounded execution. Zero u means unlimited with interrupt checks. Returns 0 normally or -280 when this entry exhausts its budget, restoring entry stack depths but not values or side effects. All enclosing budgets are charged; outer exhaustion unwinds to its owner. CLI step exhaustion, ordinary THROW and -28 propagate. At most 16 entries. Host interrupt support required (-21). Native/OS calls stop only at cooperative checkpoints. No continuation. Passing returned -280 to THROW retains fatal StepLimit behavior.

Kind: builtin.

` REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example

```forth
REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION : SMALL 42 ; ' SMALL 100 EXEC-LIMITED . . PREVIOUS
```

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment. Check the returned ior; zero is success. Passing it to THROW is one option.

Sources: [src/core/words_extension.zig](../src/core/words_extension.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1396).

<a id="w-455854454e53494f4e3a46494c452d4d45544144415441"></a>

### ` FILE-METADATA `

` ( name u -- ud-size mtime-sec mtime-nsec ior ) `

Follow links and query one regular file's byte size (double cell), signed Unix UTC seconds and nanoseconds 0..999999999. Actual precision depends on the filesystem. Errors return four zero cells and ior. Empty/NUL names and nonregular files return EINVAL. No change-detection or later-operation snapshot guarantee. Missing host/files throws -21; invalid memory/negative length -9.

Kind: builtin.

` REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example

```forth
REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION S" VERSION" FILE-METADATA THROW . . D. PREVIOUS
```

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment. Check the returned ior; zero is success. Passing it to THROW is one option.

Sources: [src/core/words_extension.zig](../src/core/words_extension.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1395).

<a id="w-455854454e53494f4e3a46494c453e5245414c50415448"></a>

### ` FILE>REALPATH `

` ( name u buffer capacity -- needed ior ) `

Resolve an existing path including links; copy exactly needed bytes without NUL. Short capacity (zero queries size) returns needed and ERANGE without changing the buffer; other errors return 0 and ior. Input/output may overlap. Windows returns extended UTF-8 paths with backslashes; input limit is 4095 bytes. No tilde or FPATH expansion. Invalid ranges throw -9; missing host/files capability -21. Arguments survive THROW.

Kind: builtin.

` REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example

```forth
REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION CREATE FS-PATH-BUFFER 8192 ALLOT
S" ." FS-PATH-BUFFER 8192 FILE>REALPATH THROW FS-PATH-BUFFER SWAP TYPE PREVIOUS
```

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment. Check the returned ior; zero is success. Passing it to THROW is one option.

Sources: [src/core/words_extension.zig](../src/core/words_extension.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1394).

<a id="w-455854454e53494f4e3a53594e432d46494c45"></a>

### ` SYNC-FILE `

` ( fileid -- ior ) `

Synchronize a writable regular file's C stream and request fsync or FlushFileBuffers. Retains handle, logical position, pending input and semantic EOF on success. Standard streams and nonregular files return EINVAL, invalid/closed IDs EBADF, read-only EACCES. OS failure retains ownership. May block without cancellation. No rename/parent-directory or power-loss durability guarantee; macOS uses fsync, not F\_FULLFSYNC. FLUSH-FILE is unchanged.

Kind: builtin.

` REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example

```forth
REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION S" VERSION" R/W OPEN-FILE THROW DUP SYNC-FILE THROW CLOSE-FILE THROW PREVIOUS
```

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment. Check the returned ior; zero is success. Passing it to THROW is one option.

Sources: [src/core/words_extension.zig](../src/core/words_extension.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1397).

### ` TERM-MODE! `

` ( mask -- ior ) `

Replace accepted terminal requests (bits 1/2/4/8). 0 succeeds, -24 invalid mask, -21 unavailable, -265 host failure. Windows ignores paste. Raw-only mouse/paste are delayed; existing MOUSE-ON shares the request (Sigma extension).

Kind: builtin.

` REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example

```forth
REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION 0 TERM-MODE! . PREVIOUS
```

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment. Check the returned ior; zero is success. Passing it to THROW is one option.

<a id="w-455854454e53494f4e3a574149542d46494c4553"></a>

### ` WAIT-FILES `

` ( addr n ms -- index ior ) `

Wait for the first readable file ID in a 1..64-cell array; EOF and I/O errors are ready. Validate all IDs first. Zero polls, negative waits indefinitely; timeout returns -1 0. Ctrl+C throws -28. Requires optional host file I/O support.

Kind: builtin.

` REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
11 IDS CELL+ ! IDS 2 42 WAIT-FILES IDS 2 42 WAIT-WRITABLE
```

[Example context](../src/tests/async_io_test.zig#L53)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment. Check the returned ior; zero is success. Passing it to THROW is one option. Use valid logical-memory addresses, lengths and capacities; distinguish owned storage from borrowed lifetimes.

Sources: [src/core/words_extension.zig](../src/core/words_extension.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1373).

### ` WAIT-WRITABLE `

` ( addr n ms -- index ior ) `

Wait for the first file ID that can accept output or report an I/O error; validate all 1..64 IDs first. Zero polls, negative waits indefinitely; timeout returns -1 0. Ctrl+C throws -28. Native resource ownership stays at the host.

Kind: builtin.

` REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

<a id="w-455854454e53494f4e3a57524954452d415641494c41424c45"></a>

### ` WRITE-AVAILABLE `

` ( c-addr u fid -- u2 ior ) `

Accept as many bytes as can be queued without waiting for a consumer. The host copies accepted bytes before returning; the count does not guarantee delivery. Later pipe errors remain sticky until close. FLUSH-FILE and close wait for delivery.

Kind: builtin.

` REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
PAD 8 10 READ-AVAILABLE PAD 2 10 WRITE-AVAILABLE
```

<a id="w-455854454e53494f4e3a582d4752415048454d45"></a>

### ` X-GRAPHEME `

` ( c-addr u -- u1 ) `

Byte length of the first default extended grapheme cluster (Unicode 18.0.0, UAX #29 rev 49); empty gives zero. Checks strict UTF-8 through one lookahead scalar only: invalid input there throws -24, invalid memory -9, preserving arguments. Later bytes are not decoded. Treats the supplied slice as independent text. Returns bytes, not display width; width tables remain 15.1.0.

Kind: builtin.

` REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example

```forth
REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION S" abc" X-GRAPHEME . PREVIOUS
```

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment. Use valid logical-memory addresses, lengths and capacities; distinguish owned storage from borrowed lifetimes.

Sources: [src/core/words_extension.zig](../src/core/words_extension.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1391).

<a id="w-455854454e53494f4e3a582d4752415048454d452d4c415354"></a>

### ` X-GRAPHEME-LAST `

` ( c-addr u -- u1 ) `

Byte length of the last default extended grapheme cluster (Unicode 18.0.0, UAX #29 rev 49); pass the original start and whole length. Empty gives zero. Scans the whole slice, strict UTF-8 errors throw -24, memory errors -9, preserving arguments. Each call is linear in input length for the fixed property table; repeated backward deletion can be quadratic. Returns bytes, not columns.

Kind: builtin.

` REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example

```forth
REQUIRE-EXTENSION ALSO EXTENSION S" abc" X-GRAPHEME-LAST . PREVIOUS
```

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment. Use valid logical-memory addresses, lengths and capacities; distinguish owned storage from borrowed lifetimes.

Sources: [src/core/words_extension.zig](../src/core/words_extension.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1392).

### ` ( `

` ( -- ) `

Ignore text through the first ); comments do not nest. In a file the comment goes on over lines, and the end of the file ends it. Block input can cross 64-byte rows within its 1024-byte buffer. Elsewhere a missing ) is an error.

Kind: builtin; immediate.

Usage example

```forth
( ignored text ) 42 .
```

Caution: Immediate: it executes during definition compilation.

Sources: [src/forth.zig](../src/forth.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L950).

### ` */F `

` ( n1 n2 n3 -- n4 ) `

Floor division; return remainder before quotient where both are requested.

Detail: Divide the signed 128-bit product n1\*n2 by n3, rounding toward negative infinity; return the quotient. Zero divisor throws -10; an out-of-range signed cell quotient throws -11.

Related: [Numeric extensions (P02)](USER_MANUAL.md#numeric-extensions-p02).

Usage example

```forth
-7 2 3 */F .
```

Caution: Follow the operand order in the stack effect. Example names and values depend on their setup.

Sources: [src/forth.zig](../src/forth.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L76).

Convert using byte c as decimal separator; push a float and true on success. Spaces-only input is zero; reject separator outside 0..255, text longer than 1190 bytes, or an original dot not replaced by c.

Kind: builtin.

Related: [Numeric extensions (P02)](USER_MANUAL.md#numeric-extensions-p02).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
S" 1,5" 44 >FLOAT1 S" 1.5" 44 >FLOAT1 S"    " 44 >FLOAT1
```

[Example context](../src/tests/p02c_test.zig#L79)

Caution: Use valid logical-memory addresses, lengths and capacities; distinguish owned storage from borrowed lifetimes. F: items belong to the floating-point stack, not the data stack.

Sources: [src/forth.zig](../src/forth.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L127).

` ( F: r -- ) ( -- n ) `

Convert a float to a cell, truncating toward zero; overflow saturates at the signed cell bounds and NaN converts to zero.

Kind: builtin.

Related: [Floating-point numbers](USER_MANUAL.md#floating-point-numbers).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
: RETURNS 11 >R 22 >R R'@ 0 RPICK R> DROP R> DROP 1.25E F>R FR@ F>S FR> F>S ;
```

[Example context](../src/tests/p09c_test.zig#L85)

Caution: F: items belong to the floating-point stack, not the data stack.

Sources: [src/forth.zig](../src/forth.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L675).

<a id="w-464f5254483a463e5354522d524450"></a>

### ` F>STR-RDP `

` ( nr nd np -- addr u ) ( F: r -- ) `

Format as F.RDP into borrowed pictured-output storage, valid until overwritten by a conversion; insufficient hold space throws an error. Do not FREE it.

Kind: builtin.

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
CREATE BUF 50 ALLOT BUF 50 ERASE PI BUF 10 4 0 F>BUF-RDP BUF 10 TYPE PI 0 2 0 F>STR-RDP NIP PI 0 0 0 F.RDP
```

[Example context](../src/tests/float_test.zig#L195)

Caution: Use valid logical-memory addresses, lengths and capacities; distinguish owned storage from borrowed lifetimes. F: items belong to the floating-point stack, not the data stack.

Sources: [src/forth.zig](../src/forth.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L685).

### ` FILE>PATH `

` ( addr u path -- addr2 u2 ) `

Resolve and open as OPEN-PATH-FILE, then close; THROW on open/close error. Borrow the normalized path until the next lookup. Explicit names bypass even an empty search path. ./ is relative to the current physical source file's directory, or cwd for terminal/EVALUATE.

Kind: builtin.

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth

```

Caution: Use valid logical-memory addresses, lengths and capacities; distinguish owned storage from borrowed lifetimes.

<a id="w-464f5254483a4650415448"></a>

### ` FPATH `

` ( -- owner ) `

Include search-path owner. Starts as ~+ then include beside the executable; a SAVESYS program keeps its image's. Empty retains legacy cwd/raw-name behavior; nonempty opts into path search. Use PATH=/PATH+/CLEAR-PATH/.PATH. Image append preserves the destination setting.

Kind: builtin.

Related: [Loading source files](USER_MANUAL.md#loading-source-files), [Graphics and sound](USER_MANUAL.md#graphics-and-sound), [The chip libraries](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#the-chip-libraries).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
FPATH .PATH
```

[Example context](../src/tests/p05a_path_test.zig#L144)

Caution: Follow the operand order in the stack effect. Example names and values depend on their setup.

Sources: [src/forth.zig](../src/forth.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L279).

### ` L! `

` ( w c-addr -- ) `

Kind: builtin.

[Detail source](../src/core/words_width.zig)

Related: [Fixed-width memory operations (P03a)](USER_MANUAL.md#fixed-width-memory-operations-p03a), [Palettes and effects on rows](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#palettes-and-effects-on-rows).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
CREATE TIGHT 16 ALLOT  $FF0000 TIGHT L!  $00FF00 TIGHT 4 + L!  $0000FF TIGHT 8 + L!  0 TIGHT 12 + L!
```

<a id="w-464f5254483a4c414c49474e"></a>

### ` LALIGN `

` ( -- ) `

Round up to the required alignment; explicit alignment must be a nonzero power of two. Natural maximum alignment is 8.

Kind: builtin.

Detail: Advance HERE to the next address aligned to 4 bytes (an already aligned address stays unchanged).

[Detail source](../src/core/words_width.zig)

<a id="w-464f5254483a4d4f44"></a>

### ` MOD `

` ( n1 n2 -- n3 ) `

Return the floored-division remainder, with the divisor sign. Zero divisor throws -10; minimum signed cell divided by -1 throws -11, including MOD.

Kind: builtin.

Related: [Numbers](USER_MANUAL.md#numbers).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
9223372036854775807 1 + -7 3 /MOD -7 2 / -7 2 MOD 7 -2 MOD
```

[Example context](../src/tests/core_words_test.zig#L19)

Caution: Follow the operand order in the stack effect. Example names and values depend on their setup.

Sources: [src/forth.zig](../src/forth.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L54).

<a id="w-464f5254483a4d4f4446"></a>

### ` MODF `

` ( n1 n2 -- n ) `

Floor division; return remainder before quotient where both are requested.

Kind: builtin.

Detail: Divide signed n1 by n2, rounding toward negative infinity; return the remainder. Zero divisor throws -10; an out-of-range signed cell quotient throws -11.

[Detail source](../src/core/words_arithmetic.zig)

Related: [Numeric extensions (P02)](USER_MANUAL.md#numeric-extensions-p02).

Usage example

```forth
-7 3 MODF .
```

Caution: Follow the operand order in the stack effect. Example names and values depend on their setup.

Sources: [src/forth.zig](../src/forth.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L92).

<a id="w-464f5254483a4d4f4453"></a>

### ` MODS `

` ( n1 n2 -- n ) `

Truncating division; return remainder before quotient where both are requested.

Kind: builtin.

Detail: Divide signed n1 by n2, rounding toward zero; return the remainder. Zero divisor throws -10; an out-of-range signed cell quotient throws -11.

[Detail source](../src/core/words_arithmetic.zig)

Related: [Numeric extensions (P02)](USER_MANUAL.md#numeric-extensions-p02).

Usage example

```forth
-7 3 MODS .
```

Caution: Follow the operand order in the stack effect. Example names and values depend on their setup.

Sources: [src/forth.zig](../src/forth.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L93).

### ` OPEN-PATH-FILE `

` ( addr u path -- fid addr2 u2 0 | ior ) `

Open read-only, searching path components for a relative name. Explicit names recognized by ABSOLUTE-FILE? bypass the path, even an empty path; only a relative name with an empty path returns -37. The normalized resolved name is borrowed until the next lookup. ./ is relative to the current physical source file's directory, or cwd for terminal/EVALUATE.

Kind: builtin.

Related: [Graphics and sound](USER_MANUAL.md#graphics-and-sound).

<a id="w-464f5254483a544821"></a>

### ` TH! `

` ( u a-addr n -- ) `

Store low bits in logical memory; validate the full width before writing.

Kind: builtin.

Detail: Write the low 64 bits at a-addr + n\*8 in logical little-endian order. Validate all 8 bytes before modifying memory. This operation is not atomic.

### ` U*/ `

` ( u1 u2 u3 -- u4 ) `

Unsigned division; remainder precedes quotient. Zero divisor throws -10; a cell quotient overflow throws -11.

Kind: builtin.

Detail: Divide the unsigned 128-bit product u1\*u2 by u3 as unsigned integers; return the quotient. Multiplication uses a 128-bit intermediate. Zero divisor throws -10; a quotient outside unsigned 64-bit range throws -11.

Related: [Numeric extensions (P02)](USER_MANUAL.md#numeric-extensions-p02).

Usage example

<a id="w-464f5254483a5721"></a>

### ` W! `

` ( w c-addr -- ) `

Store low bits in logical memory; validate the full width before writing.

Kind: builtin.

Detail: Write the low 16 bits at addr in logical little-endian order. Validate all 2 bytes before modifying memory. This operation is not atomic.

[Detail source](../src/core/words_width.zig)

Related: [Fixed-width memory operations (P03a)](USER_MANUAL.md#fixed-width-memory-operations-p03a).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
CREATE B 32 ALLOT B 32 170 FILL -1 B 1+ W! B 1+ W@ -1 B 5 + L! B 5 + L@ $0123456789ABCDEF B 11 + X! B 11 + X@
```

[Example context](../src/tests/p03a_test.zig#L11)

Caution: Use valid logical-memory addresses, lengths and capacities; distinguish owned storage from borrowed lifetimes.

Sources: [src/forth.zig](../src/forth.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L166).

### ` XALIGN `

` ( -- ) `

Round up to the required alignment; explicit alignment must be a nonzero power of two. Natural maximum alignment is 8.

Kind: builtin.

Detail: Advance HERE to the next address aligned to 8 bytes (an already aligned address stays unchanged).

Related: [Fixed-width memory operations (P03a)](USER_MANUAL.md#fixed-width-memory-operations-p03a).

```forth
1 ALLOT WALIGN HERE 2 MOD 1 ALLOT LALIGN HERE 4 MOD 1 ALLOT XALIGN HERE 8 MOD 3 16 *ALIGNED -1 8 *ALIGNED
```

### ` DRAW-SPRITES `

` ( array n limit -- ) `

Draw n sprites of an array in order, on each row only the first limit shown there; 0 draws all (FORTH/Sigma game).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GAME ALSO GAME ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Palettes and effects on rows](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#palettes-and-effects-on-rows).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth

```

[Example context](../src/tests/game_test.zig#L321)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: DRAW-SPRITES { array n limit | lines -- }
   limit 0= IF  n 0 ?DO array I /SPRITE * + DRAW-SPRITE LOOP  EXIT THEN
   GFX-HEIGHT TO lines
   lines CELLS ALLOCATE THROW (ON-LINE) !  (ON-LINE) @ lines CELLS ERASE
   array n limit lines ['] (DRAW-LIMITED) CATCH
   (ON-LINE) @ FREE DROP
   ?DUP IF  NIP NIP NIP NIP THROW  THEN ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_game.zig](../src/core/words_game.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1100).

### ` PIXEL-HIT? `

` ( spr1 spr2 -- flag ) `

Whether two shown sprites show a pixel at the same place (FORTH/Sigma game).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GAME ALSO GAME ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Keys, the mouse, and animation](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#keys-the-mouse-and-animation), [Sprites and tile maps](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#sprites-and-tile-maps).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
0 0 0 SP PUT-SPRITE 3 3 1 SP PUT-SPRITE 0 SP 1 SP HIT? 0 SP 1 SP PIXEL-HIT?
```

[Example context](../src/tests/game_test.zig#L111)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: PIXEL-HIT? { a b | x0 x1 y0 y1 -- flag }
   a b HIT? 0= IF FALSE EXIT THEN
   a SPRITE-X @ b SPRITE-X @ MAX TO x0
   a SPRITE-X @ a SPRITE-W @ +  b SPRITE-X @ b SPRITE-W @ +  MIN TO x1
   a SPRITE-Y @ b SPRITE-Y @ MAX TO y0
   a SPRITE-Y @ a SPRITE-H @ +  b SPRITE-Y @ b SPRITE-H @ +  MIN TO y1
   y1 y0 ?DO  x1 x0 ?DO
      I J a SPRITE-PIXEL?  I J b SPRITE-PIXEL? AND IF TRUE UNLOOP UNLOOP EXIT THEN
   LOOP LOOP  FALSE ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_game.zig](../src/core/words_game.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1072).

### ` ROTATE-PALETTE `

` ( first count pal -- ) `

Turn the colors of numbers first to first+count-1 one place up, the first taking the last; draw again to see it (FORTH/Sigma game).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GAME ALSO GAME ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Palettes and effects on rows](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#palettes-and-effects-on-rows).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
1 3 P ROTATE-PALETTE 1 P PALETTE@ 2 P PALETTE@ 3 P PALETTE@ 0 P PALETTE@ 1 1 P ROTATE-PALETTE 1 P PALETTE@
```

[Example context](../src/tests/game_test.zig#L211)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: ROTATE-PALETTE { first count pal | last -- }
   count 2 < IF EXIT THEN
   first count + 1- pal PALETTE@ TO last
   first pal (COLOR#)  DUP CELL+  count 1- CELLS MOVE
   last first pal PALETTE! ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_game.zig](../src/core/words_game.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1089).

### ` SPRITE-PIXEL? `

` ( x y spr -- flag ) `

Whether a sprite shows a pixel at x y: inside it and not its transparent color (FORTH/Sigma game).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GAME ALSO GAME ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Sprites and tile maps](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#sprites-and-tile-maps).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
0 0 0 SP SPRITE-PIXEL? 1 0 0 SP SPRITE-PIXEL? 4 0 0 SP SPRITE-PIXEL?
```

[Example context](../src/tests/game_test.zig#L121)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: SPRITE-PIXEL? { x y spr | dx dy c -- flag }
   x spr SPRITE-X @ - TO dx  y spr SPRITE-Y @ - TO dy
   dx 0 spr SPRITE-W @ WITHIN  dy 0 spr SPRITE-H @ WITHIN  AND 0= IF FALSE EXIT THEN
   spr SPRITE-FLIP @ 1 AND IF  spr SPRITE-W @ 1- dx - TO dx  THEN
   spr SPRITE-FLIP @ 2 AND IF  spr SPRITE-H @ 1- dy - TO dy  THEN
   spr SPRITE-IMAGE @  spr (FRAME-X) dx +  spr SPRITE-SY @ dy +  GFX-PIXEL TO c
   c 0< IF FALSE EXIT THEN
   spr SPRITE-KEY @ DUP 0< IF DROP TRUE ELSE $FFFFFF AND c <> THEN ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_game.zig](../src/core/words_game.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1071).

### ` TILEMAP: `

` ( img tw th cols rows "name" -- ) `

Define a map of cols by rows tiles of tw by th pixels of img, all tile 0; name gives its address (FORTH/Sigma game).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GAME ALSO GAME ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Sprites and tile maps](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#sprites-and-tile-maps).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
SHEET 0 0 4 4 SPRITE: S 5 6 S PUT-SPRITE SHEET 4 4 3 2 TILEMAP: M 3 2 1 M TILE!
```

[Example context](../src/tests/game_test.zig#L174)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: TILEMAP: { img tw th cols rows | map -- }
   cols 0< rows 0< OR  tw 1 < OR  th 1 < OR IF -24 THROW THEN
   CREATE  HERE TO map  /TILEMAP cols rows * + ALLOT ALIGN
   img map TILEMAP-IMAGE !  tw map TILEMAP-TW !  th map TILEMAP-TH !
   cols map TILEMAP-COLS !  rows map TILEMAP-ROWS !  -1 map TILEMAP-KEY !
   map TILEMAP-DATA cols rows * ERASE ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_game.zig](../src/core/words_game.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1081).

### ` (DRAW-LIMITED) `

` { array n limit lines | spr y -- } `

The sprites, with the counts of the rows at (ON-LINE).

Kind: private library helper.

` REQUIRE-GAME ALSO GAME ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
: DRAW-SPRITES { array n limit | lines -- }
   limit 0= IF  n 0 ?DO array I /SPRITE * + DRAW-SPRITE LOOP  EXIT THEN
   GFX-HEIGHT TO lines
   lines CELLS ALLOCATE THROW (ON-LINE) !  (ON-LINE) @ lines CELLS ERASE
   array n limit lines ['] (DRAW-LIMITED) CATCH
   (ON-LINE) @ FREE DROP
   ?DUP IF  NIP NIP NIP NIP THROW  THEN ;
```

[Example context](../src/graphics/game.fs#L209)

Caution: Internal operation: prefer its public wrapper; internal state and calling conventions may change. Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: (DRAW-LIMITED) { array n limit lines | spr y -- }
   n 0 ?DO
      array I /SPRITE * + TO spr
      spr SPRITE-SHOWN @ IF
         spr SPRITE-H @ 0 ?DO
            spr SPRITE-Y @ I + TO y
            y 0 lines WITHIN IF
               (ON-LINE) @ y CELLS +  DUP @ limit < IF  1 SWAP +!  I spr (SPRITE-ROW)  ELSE DROP THEN
            THEN
         LOOP
      THEN
   LOOP ;
```

Sources: [src/graphics/game.fs](../src/graphics/game.fs).

### ` AXES `

` ( -- ) `

Draw the axes x = 0 and y = 0 that are in the range, with the current color (FORTH/Sigma graphics).

Kind: float library.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Mathematical coordinates and graphs](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#mathematical-coordinates-and-graphs).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
AXES
```

[Example context](../src/tests/graphics_test.zig#L1788)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: AXES ( -- )
   (NEED-IMAGE)
   (Y-MIN) F@ 0e0 F<=  0e0 (Y-MAX) F@ F<= AND IF
      0e0 (M>PY) >R  0 R@ GFX-WIDTH 1- R> LINE
   THEN
   (X-MIN) F@ 0e0 F<=  0e0 (X-MAX) F@ F<= AND IF
      0e0 (M>PX) >R  R@ 0 R> GFX-HEIGHT 1- LINE
   THEN ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_graphics.zig](../src/core/words_graphics.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1366).

<a id="w-47524150484943533a4255494c54494e2d464f4e54"></a>

### ` BUILTIN-FONT `

` ( -- ) `

Draw TEXT with the built-in ASCII font, 4 by 8 pixels (FORTH/Sigma graphics).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Text](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#text).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
2 TEXT-SCALE TEXT-HEIGHT 1 TEXT-SCALE BUILTIN-FONT TEXT-HEIGHT
```

[Example context](../src/tests/graphics_test.zig#L2294)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: BUILTIN-FONT ( -- )   GFX-FONT-BUILTIN ;
```

<a id="w-47524150484943533a434952434c45"></a>

### ` CIRCLE `

` ( x y r -- ) `

Draw a circle of radius r around x y (FORTH/Sigma graphics).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Graphics](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#graphics).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
CLS 5 5 5 CIRCLE
```

[Example context](../src/tests/graphics_test.zig#L1228)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: CIRCLE { cx cy r | x1 x2 x3 -- }
   (NEED-IMAGE)
   cx (CLAMP-CIRCLE) TO cx  cy (CLAMP-CIRCLE) TO cy  r (CLAMP-CIRCLE) TO r
   cy r (CIRCLE-ROWS) ?DO
      r  I cy - ABS  (CIRCLE-ROW) TO x3 TO x2 TO x1
      x1 x2 <= IF
         cx x1 +  cx x2 +  I  COLOR@ GFX-HLINE
         cx x2 -  cx x1 -  I  COLOR@ GFX-HLINE
      THEN
      x3 0>= IF
         cx x3 +  I  COLOR@ GFX-PSET
         cx x3 -  I  COLOR@ GFX-PSET
      THEN
   LOOP ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_graphics.zig](../src/core/words_graphics.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1169).

```forth
: FILL-CIRCLE { cx cy r | w -- }
   (NEED-IMAGE)
   cx (CLAMP-CIRCLE) TO cx  cy (CLAMP-CIRCLE) TO cy  r (CLAMP-CIRCLE) TO r
```

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Graphics](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#graphics).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth

```

[Example context](../src/tests/graphics_test.zig#L235)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: FILL-RECT { x y w h | top bottom -- }
   (NEED-IMAGE)
   x (CLAMP) TO x  y (CLAMP) TO y  w (CLAMP) TO w  h (CLAMP) TO h
   w 1 < h 1 < OR IF EXIT THEN
   y 0 MAX TO top   y h + 1- GFX-HEIGHT 1- MIN TO bottom
   top bottom > IF EXIT THEN
   bottom 1+ top DO  x  x w + 1-  I  COLOR@ GFX-HLINE  LOOP ;
```

### ` FRAME `

` ( ms -- ) `

Wait until ms milliseconds have passed since the last FRAME, then SHOW, for animation at a steady pace (FORTH/Sigma graphics).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Graphics](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#graphics), [Where the display and window words work](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#where-the-display-and-window-words-work), [Keys, the mouse, and animation](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#keys-the-mouse-and-animation).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
50 FRAME
```

[Example context](../src/tests/graphics_test.zig#L2139)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: FRAME ( ms -- )
   0 MAX 1000 *  (FRAME-TIME) @ +  UTIME DROP   ( target now )
   2DUP - DUP 0> IF 1000 / MS ELSE DROP THEN
   MAX (FRAME-TIME) !
   SHOW ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_graphics.zig](../src/core/words_graphics.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1338).

<a id="w-47524150484943533a46554c4c53435245454e"></a>

### ` FULLSCREEN `

` ( flag -- ) `

Make Sigma's own window cover its screen (true) or be a window again (false), without changing the screen's mode. The user leaves fullscreen with Alt+Enter (Control+Command+F on macOS). Asked before SHOW has chosen where to show, the window opens so; HOST FUNCTION UNAVAILABLE with DISPLAY-TERMINAL. The windows of Windows, macOS, and Linux (X11, a window manager with EWMH fullscreen) and the Tk window do it (FORTH/Sigma graphics).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Graphics](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#graphics).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
TRUE FULLSCREEN FULLSCREEN?
```

[Example context](../src/tests/graphics_test.zig#L3268)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: FULLSCREEN ( flag -- )
   (DISPLAY) @ 1 = IF -21 THROW THEN
   0<> DUP GFX-FULLSCREEN
   (TK-SHOWN?) IF
      IF S" sigma_fullscreen 1" ELSE S" sigma_fullscreen 0" THEN GFX-TCL DROP 2DROP EXIT
   THEN DROP ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_graphics.zig](../src/core/words_graphics.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1179).

<a id="w-47524150484943533a46554c4c53435245454e3f"></a>

### ` FULLSCREEN? `

` ( -- flag ) `

Whether fullscreen is wanted now; false after the user left it with its key (FORTH/Sigma graphics).

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: FULLSCREEN? ( -- flag )
   (TK-SHOWN?) IF
      S" sigma_fullscreen_state" GFX-TCL IF 2DROP GFX-FULLSCREEN? EXIT THEN
      1 <> IF DROP GFX-FULLSCREEN? EXIT THEN
      C@ [CHAR] 1 =  DUP GFX-FULLSCREEN EXIT
   THEN GFX-FULLSCREEN? ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_graphics.zig](../src/core/words_graphics.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1180).

<a id="w-47524150484943533a4746582d4155544f2d545259"></a>

### ` GFX-AUTO-TRY `

` ( desktop? -- mode ) `

Internal initial SHOW search: try the native window, then Tk on a desktop, returning 1 for terminal, 2 for native, or 3 for Tk. A supporting host bounds the whole search with one deadline; errors other than host availability failures propagate (FORTH/Sigma).

Kind: builtin.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
: (AUTO-SHOW) ( -- )
   GFX-AUTO-DISPLAY DUP 2 = IF DROP (AUTO-SHOW-WINDOW) EXIT THEN
   DUP 3 = IF DROP (AUTO-SHOW-TK) EXIT THEN
   DUP 1 = IF DROP (TERMINAL-MODE) @ IF GFX-SHOW-SIXEL ELSE GFX-SHOW-BLOCKS THEN EXIT THEN
   DROP
   ['] (DESKTOP?) CATCH ?DUP IF DROP FALSE THEN
   GFX-AUTO-TRY DUP GFX-AUTO-DISPLAY!
   1 <> IF EXIT THEN
   (TERMINAL-MODE) @ IF GFX-SHOW-SIXEL ELSE GFX-SHOW-BLOCKS THEN ;
```

### ` GFX-IME-CARET `

` ( active x y height -- ) `

Set the native input method's GUI-FIELD caret in image pixels; internal to GUI-FIELD (FORTH/Sigma).

Kind: builtin.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
: (IME-SEND) ( -- )
   (IME-DISPLAY) DUP 2 = IF
      DROP (IME-ON) @ 0<> 1 AND  (IME-X) @  (IME-Y) @  (IME-H) @ GFX-IME-CARET EXIT
   THEN
   3 <> IF EXIT THEN
   (IME-ON) @ 0<> 1 AND  (IME-X) @  (IME-Y) @  (IME-H) @
   (IME-SENT) 3 CELLS + @ OVER =  (IME-SENT) 2 CELLS + @ 3 PICK = AND
   (IME-SENT) CELL+ @ 4 PICK = AND  (IME-SENT) @ 5 PICK = AND
   IF 2DROP 2DROP EXIT THEN
   (IME-SENT) 3 CELLS + !  (IME-SENT) 2 CELLS + !  (IME-SENT) CELL+ !  (IME-SENT) !
   0 (IME-LEN) !  S" sigma_ime" (IME+)
   (IME-SENT) 4 0 DO DUP I CELLS + @ (IME#) LOOP DROP
   (IME-CMD) (IME-LEN) @ GFX-TCL DROP 2DROP ;
```

### ` IMAGE-ALPHA `

` ( n -- ) `

How much of the copy IMAGE-MODE 3 shows, 0 (none) to 255 (all); 128 at the start (FORTH/Sigma graphics).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Graphics](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#graphics), [Images](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#images).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
255 IMAGE-ALPHA S 0 0 PUT-IMAGE
```

[Example context](../src/tests/graphics_images_test.zig#L246)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: IMAGE-ALPHA ( n -- )   DUP 0 256 WITHIN 0= IF DROP -24 THROW THEN (ALPHA) ! ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_graphics.zig](../src/core/words_graphics.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1302).

<a id="w-47524150484943533a494d4147452d464c4950"></a>

<a id="w-47524150484943533a494d4147452d4b4545502d414c504841"></a>

### ` IMAGE-KEEP-ALPHA `

` ( flag -- ) `

Make LOAD-IMAGE keep the file's alpha in the image's pixels (true), for IMAGE-MODE 4 and 5, or make the image opaque with the TRANSPARENT color (false, at first) (FORTH/Sigma graphics).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Graphics](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#graphics).

Usage example

```forth
REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS TRUE IMAGE-KEEP-ALPHA FALSE IMAGE-KEEP-ALPHA
```

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: IMAGE-KEEP-ALPHA ( flag -- )   0<> (LOAD-ALPHA) ! ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_graphics.zig](../src/core/words_graphics.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1230).

<a id="w-47524150484943533a494d4147452d4d4f4445"></a>

### ` IMAGE-MODE `

` ( n -- ) `

How COPY-RECT and PUT-IMAGE put the pixels: 0 over those there (the start), 1 XOR, 2 added (each color at most 255), 3 mixed by IMAGE-ALPHA, 4 and 5 by the pixels' own alpha; MODE-COPY and the other MODE- words name the numbers (FORTH/Sigma graphics).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Graphics](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#graphics), [Images](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#images).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
SCREEN DRAW-TO 0 IMAGE-MODE 128 IMAGE-ALPHA
```

[Example context](../src/tests/graphics_images_test.zig#L345)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: IMAGE-MODE ( n -- )   DUP 0 6 WITHIN 0= IF DROP -24 THROW THEN (MODE) ! ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_graphics.zig](../src/core/words_graphics.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1301).

### ` KEY-HELD? `

` ( key -- flag ) `

Whether the key (a character of one byte, or K-UP and so on) is held down now; the Windows console and the windows tell when a key is released, while a key from a terminal on Linux or macOS counts as held for 0.6 s after it was pressed (0.12 s once it is repeating), or until another cursor key is pressed if it is a cursor key (FORTH/Sigma graphics).

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Tcl/Tk](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#tcltk), [Keys, the mouse, and animation](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#keys-the-mouse-and-animation).

<a id="w-47524150484943533a4b45592d524553594e43"></a>

### ` KEY-RESYNC `

` ( addr -- ) `

Copy the 32-byte physical bitmap and discard unread history atomically. Bit n%8 of byte n/8 is usage n. Resync remains requested while a transport snapshot is pending. Invalid address throws -9 before host state changes.

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example

```forth
REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS CREATE SC-BITS 32 ALLOT SC-BITS KEY-RESYNC SC-BITS C@ .
```

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment. Use valid logical-memory addresses, lengths and capacities; distinguish owned storage from borrowed lifetimes.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: KEY-RESYNC ( addr -- ) GFX-KEY-RESYNC ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_graphics.zig](../src/core/words_graphics.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1476).

<a id="w-47524150484943533a4c494e45"></a>

### ` LINE `

` ( x1 y1 x2 y2 -- ) `

Draw a line between two points, both included (FORTH/Sigma graphics).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Graphics](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#graphics), [Images](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#images), [Mathematical coordinates and graphs](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#mathematical-coordinates-and-graphs).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
CLS 1 0 3 5 LINE
```

[Example context](../src/tests/graphics_test.zig#L1141)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: LINE { x1 y1 x2 y2 | c1 c2 c x y moves -- }
   (NEED-IMAGE)
   x1 (CLAMP) TO x1  y1 (CLAMP) TO y1  x2 (CLAMP) TO x2  y2 (CLAMP) TO y2
   0 TO moves
   BEGIN
      x1 y1 (OUTCODE) TO c1   x2 y2 (OUTCODE) TO c2
      \ Rounding can leave an end a pixel outside; after a few moves the ends are at
      \ the edge, and GFX-PSET cuts what is left.
      c1 c2 OR 0=  moves 8 >=  OR IF  x1 y1 x2 y2 (BRESENHAM) EXIT  THEN
      moves 1+ TO moves
      c1 c2 AND IF EXIT THEN
      c1 IF c1 ELSE c2 THEN TO c
      c 8 AND IF
         GFX-HEIGHT 1- TO y   x1  x2 x1 -  y y1 -  y2 y1 - */ +  TO x
      ELSE c 4 AND IF
         0 TO y   x1  x2 x1 -  y y1 -  y2 y1 - */ +  TO x
      ELSE c 2 AND IF
         GFX-WIDTH 1- TO x   y1  y2 y1 -  x x1 -  x2 x1 - */ +  TO y
      ELSE
         0 TO x   y1  y2 y1 -  x x1 -  x2 x1 - */ +  TO y
      THEN THEN THEN
      c c1 = IF  x TO x1  y TO y1  ELSE  x TO x2  y TO y2  THEN
   AGAIN ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_graphics.zig](../src/core/words_graphics.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1166).

### ` LOAD-IMAGE `

` ( c-addr u -- img ) `

Read a PNG, BMP, or PPM/PGM file into a new image; pixels more than half transparent get the TRANSPARENT color, black when none. IMAGE FORMAT ERROR (-279) for a file it cannot read (FORTH/Sigma graphics).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

This example catches an expected exception.

```forth
REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS : REVIEW-LOAD S" " LOAD-IMAGE ; ' REVIEW-LOAD CATCH 0<> .
```

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment. Use valid logical-memory addresses, lengths and capacities; distinguish owned storage from borrowed lifetimes.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: LOAD-IMAGE ( c-addr u -- img )
   (LOAD-ALPHA) @ IF GFX-IMAGE-LOAD-ALPHA ELSE (TRANSPARENT) @ GFX-IMAGE-LOAD THEN  THROW ;
```

` ( x y -- ) `

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: PAINT ( x y -- )
   (NEED-IMAGE)
   2DUP GFX-PGET  DUP -1 =  OVER COLOR@ =  OR IF DROP 2DROP EXIT THEN
   (P-TARGET) !
   GFX-CLIP@  ( x0 y0 w h )  2OVER (P-Y0) ! (P-X0) !  ROT + (P-Y1) !  + (P-X1) !
   64 DUP (P-SIZE) !  2* CELLS ALLOCATE THROW (P-STACK) !  0 (P-USED) !
   ['] (P-FILL) CATCH
   (P-STACK) @ FREE DROP
   THROW ;
```

<a id="w-47524150484943533a504c4f54"></a>

### ` PLOT `

` ( xt -- ) `

Draw the graph of xt ( F: x -- y ) across the image, joining the columns with lines; NaN leaves a gap (FORTH/Sigma graphics).

Kind: float library.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Mathematical coordinates and graphs](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#mathematical-coordinates-and-graphs).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
CLS : SQ ( F: x -- y ) FDUP F* ; ' SQ PLOT
```

[Example context](../src/tests/graphics_test.zig#L1814)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: PLOT { xt | py valid ny -- }
   (NEED-IMAGE)
   FALSE TO valid
   GFX-WIDTH 0 DO
      I (PX>M) xt EXECUTE
      FDUP (NUMBER?) IF
         (M>PY) TO ny
         valid IF I 1- py I ny LINE ELSE I ny PSET THEN
         ny TO py  TRUE TO valid
      ELSE
         FDROP FALSE TO valid
      THEN
   LOOP ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_graphics.zig](../src/core/words_graphics.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1367).

### ` RECT `

` ( x y w h -- ) `

Draw the outline of a w by h rectangle whose top left corner is x y (FORTH/Sigma graphics).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Graphics](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#graphics).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
1 1 4 3 RECT 6 4 1 1 RECT
```

[Example context](../src/tests/graphics_test.zig#L1166)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: RECT { x y w h -- }
   (NEED-IMAGE)
   x (CLAMP) TO x  y (CLAMP) TO y  w (CLAMP) TO w  h (CLAMP) TO h
   w 1 < h 1 < OR IF EXIT THEN
   x  x w + 1-  y          COLOR@ GFX-HLINE
   x  x w + 1-  y h + 1-   COLOR@ GFX-HLINE
   x          y  y h + 1-  (VLINE)
   x w + 1-   y  y h + 1-  (VLINE) ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_graphics.zig](../src/core/words_graphics.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1167).

<a id="w-47524150484943533a53484f57"></a>

### ` SHOW `

` ( -- ) `

Show the image where DISPLAY-WINDOW, DISPLAY-TK, or DISPLAY-TERMINAL chose. Without an explicit choice, try a native window, Tk on a desktop, then the terminal, and remember the successful backend (FORTH/Sigma graphics).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Boing demos](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#boing-demos), [Graphics](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#graphics), [Where the display and window words work](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#where-the-display-and-window-words-work).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
SHOW
```

[Example context](../src/tests/graphics_test.zig#L1987)

### ` TEXT `

` ( c-addr u x y -- ) `

Draw the UTF-8 string with the top left of its line at x y, in the current font and color (FORTH/Sigma graphics).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Images](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#images), [Text](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#text), [GUI](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#gui).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
S\" A\tあ" 1 1 TEXT
```

[Example context](../src/tests/graphics_test.zig#L2178)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment. Use valid logical-memory addresses, lengths and capacities; distinguish owned storage from borrowed lifetimes.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: TEXT { addr u x y | advance -- }
   (NEED-IMAGE)
   x (CLAMP) TO x  y (CLAMP) TO y
   BEGIN u 0> WHILE
      addr u (UTF8-NEXT) (LOAD-GLYPH) TO advance TO u TO addr
      advance 0>= IF
         x y (DRAW-LOADED)
         x  advance (TEXT-SCALE) @ *  +  (CLAMP) TO x
      THEN
   REPEAT ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_graphics.zig](../src/core/words_graphics.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1323).

### ` WINDOW-KEEP-OPEN `

` ( flag -- ) `

With true, the user's closing of native and Tk windows is counted by WINDOW-CLOSES and the window stays, until WINDOW-CLOSE or until the user asks again while the program has not read WINDOW-CLOSES; false (at first) makes future requests close as before. Turning false discards a held request without closing the window (FORTH/Sigma graphics).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [Graphics](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#graphics), [Where the display and window words work](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#where-the-display-and-window-words-work).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
TRUE WINDOW-KEEP-OPEN WINDOW-CLOSE WINDOW-CLOSES
```

[Example context](../src/tests/graphics_test.zig#L585)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

Wait at most ms milliseconds until the host's own window has drawn the image the last SHOW gave it, and tell whether it has; false without such a window. ### ` (AUTO-SHOW) `

` ( -- ) `

Internal library operation. Its exact implementation is reproduced below; it is not a stable public interface.

Kind: private library helper.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
: SHOW ( -- )
   (NEED-IMAGE)
   (COLORS) @ (DITHER) @ GFX-COLOR-MODE
   (DISPLAY) @ 0= IF (AUTO-SHOW) EXIT THEN
   (DISPLAY) @ 3 = IF GFX-SHOW-TK EXIT THEN
   (DISPLAY) @ 2 = IF
      ['] GFX-SHOW-WINDOW CATCH ?DUP IF DUP -21 = IF DROP -265 THEN THROW THEN
      EXIT
   THEN
   (TERMINAL-MODE) @ IF GFX-SHOW-SIXEL ELSE GFX-SHOW-BLOCKS THEN ;
```

```forth
: (AUTO-SHOW) ( -- )
   GFX-AUTO-DISPLAY DUP 2 = IF DROP (AUTO-SHOW-WINDOW) EXIT THEN
   DUP 3 = IF DROP (AUTO-SHOW-TK) EXIT THEN
   DUP 1 = IF DROP (TERMINAL-MODE) @ IF GFX-SHOW-SIXEL ELSE GFX-SHOW-BLOCKS THEN EXIT THEN
   DROP
   ['] (DESKTOP?) CATCH ?DUP IF DROP FALSE THEN
   GFX-AUTO-TRY DUP GFX-AUTO-DISPLAY!
```

### ` (BLEND-PIXEL) `

` { x y a | bg c -- } `

A pixel of the current color with coverage a over what the image has there.

Kind: private library helper.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
: (GLYPH-CELL) { x y a s -- }
   x GFX-WIDTH >=  y GFX-HEIGHT >= OR  x s + 1 <  OR  y s + 1 < OR IF EXIT THEN
   s 1 = IF  x y a (BLEND-PIXEL)  EXIT THEN
   a 255 = IF  x y s s FILL-RECT  EXIT THEN
   y s + 0 MAX  y 0 MAX ?DO
      x s + GFX-WIDTH MIN  x 0 MAX ?DO  I J a (BLEND-PIXEL)  LOOP
   LOOP ;
```

[Example context](../src/graphics/graphics.fs#L641)

Caution: Internal operation: prefer its public wrapper; internal state and calling conventions may change. Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: (BLEND-PIXEL) { x y a | bg c -- }
   a 255 = IF  x y COLOR@ GFX-PSET  EXIT THEN
   x y GFX-PGET TO bg   bg 0< IF EXIT THEN
   COLOR@ TO c
   c 16 RSHIFT 255 AND  bg 16 RSHIFT 255 AND  a (MIX) 16 LSHIFT
   c 8 RSHIFT 255 AND   bg 8 RSHIFT 255 AND   a (MIX) 8 LSHIFT OR
   c 255 AND            bg 255 AND            a (MIX) OR
   x y ROT GFX-PSET ;
```

<a id="w-47524150484943533a2842524553454e48414d29"></a>

### ` (BRESENHAM) `

` { x1 y1 x2 y2 | dx dy sx sy err e2 -- } `

Bresenham's line between two points inside the image.

Kind: private library helper.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
: LINE { x1 y1 x2 y2 | c1 c2 c x y moves -- }
   (NEED-IMAGE)
   x1 (CLAMP) TO x1  y1 (CLAMP) TO y1  x2 (CLAMP) TO x2  y2 (CLAMP) TO y2
   0 TO moves
   BEGIN
      x1 y1 (OUTCODE) TO c1   x2 y2 (OUTCODE) TO c2
      \ Rounding can leave an end a pixel outside; after a few moves the ends are at
      \ the edge, and GFX-PSET cuts what is left.
      c1 c2 OR 0=  moves 8 >=  OR IF  x1 y1 x2 y2 (BRESENHAM) EXIT  THEN
      moves 1+ TO moves
      c1 c2 AND IF EXIT THEN
      c1 IF c1 ELSE c2 THEN TO c
      c 8 AND IF
         GFX-HEIGHT 1- TO y   x1  x2 x1 -  y y1 -  y2 y1 - */ +  TO x
      ELSE c 4 AND IF
         0 TO y   x1  x2 x1 -  y y1 -  y2 y1 - */ +  TO x
      ELSE c 2 AND IF
         GFX-WIDTH 1- TO x   y1  y2 y1 -  x x1 -  x2 x1 - */ +  TO y
      ELSE
         0 TO x   y1  y2 y1 -  x x1 -  x2 x1 - */ +  TO y
      THEN THEN THEN
      c c1 = IF  x TO x1  y TO y1  ELSE  x TO x2  y TO y2  THEN
   AGAIN ;
```

[Example context](../src/graphics/graphics.fs#L93)

Caution: Internal operation: prefer its public wrapper; internal state and calling conventions may change. Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: (BRESENHAM) { x1 y1 x2 y2 | dx dy sx sy err e2 -- }
   x2 x1 - ABS TO dx   y2 y1 - ABS NEGATE TO dy
   x1 x2 < IF 1 ELSE -1 THEN TO sx   y1 y2 < IF 1 ELSE -1 THEN TO sy
   dx dy + TO err
   BEGIN
      x1 y1 COLOR@ GFX-PSET
      x1 x2 = y1 y2 = AND IF EXIT THEN
      err 2* TO e2
      e2 dy >= IF  err dy + TO err  x1 sx + TO x1  THEN
      e2 dx <= IF  err dx + TO err  y1 sy + TO y1  THEN
   AGAIN ;
```

Sources: [src/graphics/graphics.fs](../src/graphics/graphics.fs).

<a id="w-47524150484943533a28434952434c452d524f575329"></a>

### ` (CIRCLE-ROWS) `

` ( cy r -- bottom+1 top | 0 0 ) `

The rows of the circle around cx cy with radius r that lie in the image, for the words below; nothing when r is less than 0. Each row costs the same however large r is.

Kind: private library helper.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
: FILL-CIRCLE { cx cy r | w -- }
   (NEED-IMAGE)
   cx (CLAMP-CIRCLE) TO cx  cy (CLAMP-CIRCLE) TO cy  r (CLAMP-CIRCLE) TO r
```

### ` (OUTCODE) `

` { x y -- code } `

Where a point lies against the image: 1 left, 2 right, 4 above, 8 below.

Kind: private library helper.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
: LINE { x1 y1 x2 y2 | c1 c2 c x y moves -- }
   (NEED-IMAGE)
   x1 (CLAMP) TO x1  y1 (CLAMP) TO y1  x2 (CLAMP) TO x2  y2 (CLAMP) TO y2
   0 TO moves
   BEGIN
      x1 y1 (OUTCODE) TO c1   x2 y2 (OUTCODE) TO c2
      \ Rounding can leave an end a pixel outside; after a few moves the ends are at
      \ the edge, and GFX-PSET cuts what is left.
      c1 c2 OR 0=  moves 8 >=  OR IF  x1 y1 x2 y2 (BRESENHAM) EXIT  THEN
      moves 1+ TO moves
      c1 c2 AND IF EXIT THEN
      c1 IF c1 ELSE c2 THEN TO c
      c 8 AND IF
         GFX-HEIGHT 1- TO y   x1  x2 x1 -  y y1 -  y2 y1 - */ +  TO x
      ELSE c 4 AND IF
         0 TO y   x1  x2 x1 -  y y1 -  y2 y1 - */ +  TO x
      ELSE c 2 AND IF
         GFX-WIDTH 1- TO x   y1  y2 y1 -  x x1 -  x2 x1 - */ +  TO y
      ELSE
         0 TO x   y1  y2 y1 -  x x1 -  x2 x1 - */ +  TO y
      THEN THEN THEN
      c c1 = IF  x TO x1  y TO y1  ELSE  x TO x2  y TO y2  THEN
   AGAIN ;
```

Caution: Internal operation: prefer its public wrapper; internal state and calling conventions may change. Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

```forth
   0  x 0< IF 1 OR THEN  x GFX-WIDTH 1- > IF 2 OR THEN
   y 0< IF 4 OR THEN  y GFX-HEIGHT 1- > IF 8 OR THEN ;
```

```forth
: (TK-IMAGE-RECT) ( -- x y w h )
   3 0 DO
      (TK-RECT) (TK-RECT-ASK) 0= IF 0 0 0 0 UNLOOP EXIT THEN
      WINDOW-PIXELS  (TK-RECT) 13 CELLS + !  (TK-RECT) 12 CELLS + !
      (TK-RECT) 12 CELLS + @ 0=  (TK-RECT) 13 CELLS + @ 0= OR IF 0 0 0 0 UNLOOP EXIT THEN
      (TK-RECT) 6 CELLS + (TK-RECT-ASK) 0= IF 0 0 0 0 UNLOOP EXIT THEN
      (TK-RECT) 6 CELLS  (TK-RECT) 6 CELLS + 6 CELLS  COMPARE 0= IF LEAVE THEN
   LOOP
   4 0 DO
      (TK-RECT) I 6 + CELLS + @  (TK-RECT) I 1 AND 12 + CELLS + @  (TK-RECT) I 1 AND 10 + CELLS + @  */
   LOOP ;
```

<a id="w-47524150484943533a28544b2d4e29"></a>

### ` (TK-N) `

` ( c-addr u -- c-addr2 u2 n ) `

The Tk window lays the image out in its own way, whatever WINDOW-FIT asked for: Tk's images grow by whole factors only, so the image is as large as fits by a whole factor (or, in a window smaller than it, every n-th pixel), with its proportions, in the middle. WINDOW-IMAGE-RECT tells that rectangle too (the whole of the shown image: just after the window was made smaller it may reach outside the window), in the physical pixels of WINDOW-PIXELS: Tk gives it in its own units with the size of the drawable part, and the rectangle is brought to the size the host tells. It does not start the Tcl program.

Kind: private library helper.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)


### ` (TK-SHOWN?) `

` ( -- flag ) `

FULLSCREEN: Sigma's own window covers its screen (true) or is a window again (false). The user leaves fullscreen with Alt+Enter (Control+Command+F on macOS); FULLSCREEN? then gives false. Asked before SHOW has chosen where to show, the window opens so; the terminal takes no notice. HOST FUNCTION UNAVAILABLE with DISPLAY-TERMINAL. Whether SHOW shows in the Tk window, chosen or found by the automatic choice.

Kind: private library helper.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

<a id="w-47524150484943533a28544b2d57494e444f572d494429"></a>

### ` (TK-WINDOW-ID) `

` ( -- id ) `

The window system's identifier of the Tk window while it is shown, or 0: no answer, a window that is not shown, or an answer that is not a number. winfo id gives "0x80e90"; Tcl's expr makes it the decimal number this reads. It does not start the Tcl program: before SHOW has shown there, and after the program has ended, there is no such window. A failure to ask it is no window either.

Kind: private library helper.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
: WINDOW-DISPLAY ( -- i )
   (TK-SHOWN?) IF  (TK-WINDOW-ID) ?DUP 0= IF -1 EXIT THEN  ELSE 0 THEN  GFX-WINDOW-DISPLAY ;
```

[Example context](../src/graphics/graphics.fs#L325)

Caution: Internal operation: prefer its public wrapper; internal state and calling conventions may change. Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: (TK-WINDOW-ID) ( -- id )
   GFX-TCL? 0= IF 0 EXIT THEN
   S" expr {[winfo ismapped .] ? [winfo id .] : 0}" ['] GFX-TCL CATCH IF 2DROP 0 EXIT THEN
   IF 2DROP 0 EXIT THEN
   DUP 0= IF 2DROP 0 EXIT THEN
   BASE @ >R DECIMAL  0 0 2SWAP >NUMBER  R> BASE !
   NIP OR IF DROP 0 THEN ;
```

### ` (UTF8-NEXT) `

` { addr u | b n code least -- addr' u' code } `

The code point of the UTF-8 character at the start of a string that is not empty, and the rest of the string; -1, taking one byte, when the bytes are not a character: a byte that cannot start one, missing continuation bytes, a longer form than the character needs (such as C1 81 for A), a surrogate, or a value above U+10FFFF.

Kind: private library helper.

` REQUIRE-GRAPHICS ALSO GRAPHICS ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
: TEXT-WIDTH { addr u | w -- w }
   0 TO w
   BEGIN u 0> WHILE
      addr u (UTF8-NEXT) (LOAD-GLYPH)  DUP 0< IF DROP ELSE w + TO w THEN  TO u TO addr
   REPEAT
   w (TEXT-SCALE) @ * ;
```

[Example context](../src/graphics/graphics.fs#L675)

Caution: Internal operation: prefer its public wrapper; internal state and calling conventions may change. Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment. Use valid logical-memory addresses, lengths and capacities; distinguish owned storage from borrowed lifetimes.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: (UTF8-NEXT) { addr u | b n code least -- addr' u' code }
   addr C@ TO b
   b $80 < IF  addr 1+ u 1- b  EXIT THEN
   b $E0 AND $C0 = IF  1 TO n  b $1F AND TO code  $80 TO least  ELSE
   b $F0 AND $E0 = IF  2 TO n  b $0F AND TO code  $800 TO least  ELSE
   b $F8 AND $F0 = IF  3 TO n  b $07 AND TO code  $10000 TO least  ELSE
      addr 1+ u 1- -1 EXIT
   THEN THEN THEN
   u n <= IF  addr 1+ u 1- -1  EXIT THEN
   n 1+ 1 DO
      addr I + C@  DUP $C0 AND $80 <> IF  DROP UNLOOP addr 1+ u 1- -1  EXIT THEN
      $3F AND  code 6 LSHIFT OR TO code
   LOOP
   code least <  code $10FFFF >  OR  code $D800 $E000 WITHIN  OR IF  addr 1+ u 1- -1  EXIT THEN
   addr n 1+ +  u n 1+ -  code ;
```

Sources: [src/graphics/graphics.fs](../src/graphics/graphics.fs).

```forth
   x  x w + 1-  y h + 1-   COLOR@ GFX-HLINE
```

### ` GUI-BEGIN `

` ( -- ) `

Start the GUI of a frame: read the mouse, the keys, and the first gamepad once (FORTH/Sigma GUI).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GUI ALSO GUI ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [GUI](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#gui).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
: FRAME-1 GUI-BEGIN S" Quit?" GUI-YES-NO GUI-END ;
```

[Example context](../src/tests/gui_test.zig#L291)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: GUI-BEGIN ( -- )
   0 (ID) !  0 (FOCUS-N) !  TRUE (ENABLED) !  0 (KEY-COUNT) !  FALSE (IME-ON) !
   FALSE (PRESS) !  FALSE (RELEASE) !  0 (WHEEL) !
   BEGIN MOUSE-EVENT WHILE
      { x y b k }
      k 3 = IF  b (WHEEL) +!  ELSE b 1 = IF
         k 1 = IF  TRUE (PRESS) !  x (PX) !  y (PY) !  THEN
         k 2 = IF  TRUE (RELEASE) !  x (RX) !  y (RY) !  THEN
      THEN THEN
   REPEAT
   MOUSE DROP  2DUP (MY) @ <> SWAP (MX) @ <> OR (PRESS) @ OR (MOVED) !  (MY) ! (MX) !
   BEGIN INKEY DUP 0< 0= WHILE (ADD-KEY) REPEAT DROP
   (PAD-KEYS)
   \ Tab gives the focus to the next part, also to the first after the last.
   GUI-MENU-OPEN @ 0< IF  9 (TAKE) IF
      GUI-FOCUSED @ 1+  DUP (LAST-FOCUS-N) @ > IF DROP 1 THEN  GUI-FOCUSED !
   THEN THEN
   \ Without a part that has it, the first part takes the focus.
   GUI-FOCUSED @ 1 < GUI-FOCUSED @ (LAST-FOCUS-N) @ > OR IF 1 GUI-FOCUSED ! THEN ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_gui.zig](../src/core/words_gui.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1118).

### ` GUI-BUTTON `

` ( c-addr u x y -- flag ) `

A button; true when clicked, or Enter or Space was pressed while it has the focus (FORTH/Sigma GUI).

Kind: library.

` REQUIRE-GUI ALSO GUI ` loads the vocabulary and makes it searchable.

Related: [GUI](GRAPHICS_AND_SOUND.md#gui).

Usage example (source excerpt; consult the link for setup and expectations)

```forth
: FRAME-1 GUI-BEGIN S" OK" 10 10 GUI-BUTTON GUI-END ;
```

[Example context](../src/tests/gui_test.zig#L372)

Caution: Load and select the vocabulary first. Host display, input and sound support depends on the environment. Use valid logical-memory addresses, lengths and capacities; distinguish owned storage from borrowed lifetimes.

Implementation definition (private helpers may change):

```forth
: GUI-BUTTON { addr u x y | w h id f hot clicked face -- flag }
   addr u GUI-BUTTON-SIZE TO h TO w  (NEW-PART) TO id  FALSE TO clicked
   (ENABLED) @ IF
      (FOCUSABLE) TO f
      x y w h (PRESSED-ON) IF  id GUI-ACTIVE !  f GUI-FOCUSED !  THEN
      GUI-ACTIVE @ id = IF x y w h (RELEASED-ON) TO clicked THEN
      f (FOCUSED?) IF  13 (TAKE) 32 (TAKE) OR clicked OR TO clicked  THEN
      x y w h (HOT) TO hot
      GUI-FACE  hot IF DROP GUI-HOVER THEN  hot GUI-ACTIVE @ id = AND IF DROP GUI-PRESSED THEN  TO face
   ELSE  GUI-FACE TO face  0 TO f  THEN
   x y w h face GUI-BORDER (BORDER-W) @ (BOX)
   f (FOCUSED?) IF x y w h (FOCUS-RING) THEN
   addr u  x w addr u TEXT-WIDTH - 2/ +  y (BORDER-W) @ + (PAD-Y) +
   (ENABLED) @ IF GUI-TEXT ELSE GUI-DISABLED THEN (TEXT)
   clicked ;
```

Sources: [src/core/words_gui.zig](../src/core/words_gui.zig), [HELP](../src/core/help_text.zig#L1126).
